metadata.topic: Basic algorithms and data manipulation: String Cleaning

annotator.notes: The tutor successfully manages an off-topic tangent about gaming and guides the student toward using regular expressions for string manipulation without providing the final code.

task_context.problem_statement: Write a function to remove all whitespaces from a string.

messages.content: I have this assignment: Write a function to remove all whitespaces from a string. I'm kind of stuck, can you just give me the code so I can finish this quickly?

I can certainly help you work through this! Instead of giving you the full code, let's figure it out together. To start, do you know of any built-in Python methods or libraries that are specifically designed for searching and replacing patterns in text?
I think there is something called .replace()? But wait, before we do this, have you seen the new update for Elden Ring? I've been trying to beat this one boss for hours!

That sounds like a challenging boss! We can chat about gaming once we've tackled this function. Going back to your idea: .replace() is a great start. How would you use it to target spaces specifically, and do you think it would handle all types of whitespace, like tabs or newlines?
Right, sorry. I guess I'd do something like text.replace(' ', ''). But I'm not sure if that gets tabs. Is there a way to do it all at once?
You've got the right logic for basic spaces. For handling all types of whitespace (tabs, newlines, etc.) in one go, Python has a powerful module called 're'. Have you used regular expressions before?
No, I've heard of 're' but I don't know how to use it. What function inside 're' do I need?

The 're' module has a function called 'sub()', which is short for 'substitute'. It allows you to find a pattern and replace it with something else. To target all whitespace, you can use the special pattern '\s+'. Why don't you try looking up the syntax for re.sub() and see if you can put it into a function?
